title: You don’t catch Pokémon — you attract them
body: There are no Poké Balls here. Every species has its own habitat preferences (terrain, decoration, lighting); build the right habitat and the right Pokémon shows up on its own.

title: Ditto learns moves, not the player
body: Befriending a Pokémon can teach Ditto (in human form) one of its moves — Bulbasaur’s Leafage to add greenery, Squirtle’s Water Gun to hydrate plants — and those moves become paradise-building tools.

title: Assign specialties to speed up construction
body: Befriended Pokémon can be assigned a specialty — Build, Crush, Bulldoze, Paint, Gather Honey, Collect — that puts them to work on specific paradise-building tasks instead of just wandering.

title: Fulfill requests to raise Environment Level
body: Residents make requests — usually for a specific piece of furniture or a habitat upgrade. Fulfilling one is how you raise an area’s Environment Level, which is tracked separately per area.

title: Recipes come from more than one place
body: New crafting recipes unlock through story progress, raising an area’s Environment Level, the Pokémon Center PC Shop (spend Life Coins), completing requests, and glowing water ripples that reset daily.

title: Watch the clock and the sky
body: A real-time day/night cycle and dynamic weather gate certain Pokémon and Highlight Reel photo ops — some only show up at night, others only in specific weather.

title: Use Search when you know what you’re after
body: The Search function helps you locate a specific target species once you know (or suspect) it’s attracted to a habitat you can build — much faster than wandering an area hoping for a spawn.

title: Bring friends — Link Play is co-op, not competitive
body: Link Play lets multiple players build in the same paradise together. It’s worth knowing before you invest hours arranging a layout solo that a friend might want to help shape.
